history.dynasty: Gurjara-Pratihara; commissioned under feudatory Maharajadhiraj Parmeshwara Mathanadeva
history.summary: The Neelkanth (Nilkantheshwar) Mahadev Temple stands on a hill at Tehla village in Rajgarh tehsil, Alwar district, inside the buffer zone of the Sariska Tiger Reserve. It was built between the 6th and 9th centuries by Maharajadhiraj Parmeshwara Mathanadeva, a feudatory of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire (per an inscription dated 961 CE); the local Pratihara line later became known as the Badgujar. The site was anciently called Rajyapura and later Paranagar, and the surviving temple gives its name to a group of over a dozen shrines, said to be the sole intact one amid the ruins of some 200. It is trikuta (three sanctums) with an intact nagara shikhara over the central sanctum and richly sculpted pancharatha outer walls (Harihara, Narasimha, Tripurantaka, surasundaris, mithuna, dikpalas; erotic panels in Khajuraho style noted). Legends link a Shivalinga to the Pandavas (brought from Kashi) and tell of Aurangzeb's troops being repelled by swarms of bees (folklore - verify). The linga remains in active worship. name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
town: Tehla village, Rajgarh tehsil (CSV town 'Alwar' is approximate - ~72 km away)
town_description: Tehla is a village in Rajgarh tehsil of Alwar district, Rajasthan, on the edge of the Aravalli hills at the boundary of the Sariska Tiger Reserve's buffer zone. The Neelkanth temple complex sits on a hill above the village, reached by a steep track; the wider area was the early-medieval temple town of Rajyapura/Paranagar, whose ruins of some 200 temples still dot the landscape.
